findings.issue: A0 grants without the effective realU accepted-three-target barrier. _md_reconcile may clear accepted during target cancellation/replacement and create targets awaiting native ACK, but _a0_check proceeds. Original _md_check lines162-163 explicitly requires all three accepted. Existing BTC_REDUCE targets are correctly not treated as debt, but their current accepted generation still must be authoritative.
findings.correction: Require known current accepted target generation and actual complete remaining native TP protection before A0 grant/submit; UNKNOWN or cancel/replacement ACK blocks. Reuse existing realU semantics, no new protection model. Add delayed/cancelled target-ACK assertion within an existing fixture and prove no grant until all accepted.

findings.issue: After risk cancel the split parent remains closed. Ordinary TP invokes _split_stop, _a0_stop only marks dead, then _split_stop returns immediately for closed parent. A live released child therefore is not cancelled in the TP fill callback; next _pair_quote cancels only after native matching/fill delivery, allowing a preventable post-TP increase. Current A03 covers TP before release and other release cases fill the entire child before TP, so none expose this ordering.
findings.correction: On ordinary stop, cancel any live/inflight A0-owned release immediately even when historical split parent is already closed; keep old native history closed, preserve one attempt, reconcile actual cancel-race fills/caps. Strengthen one existing instance to cover release resting/partial -> actual ordinary TP -> immediate cancel -> terminal ACK/late fill handling without an additional engine.
